assumptions.assumption: the host sequences commands; the master does no address decoding of its own.
assumptions.reason: the request is for byte-level commands, so any register sequence can be tried.

assumptions.assumption: data commands on a free bus are ignored rather than starting the bus.
assumptions.reason: keeps every bus condition explicit in the command stream.

behaviour: A write to CMD while BUSY = 0 starts one command - OP = CMD[2:0] - 1 START, 2 WRITE (byte CMD[15:8]), 3 READ (CMD[16] = 1 answers NACK, 0 answers ACK), 4 STOP.
Ignored (no bus activity, no register change) - a CMD write while BUSY = 1, any other OP value, WRITE / READ / STOP while the bus is not owned.
BUSY is 1 from the CMD write until the command's last step has finished.
The bus is owned from the end of a START until a STOP.

Q = QUARTER clocks. Releasing SCL is followed by waiting until SCL is seen high through the two-flop synchroniser (a stretching slave holds it low); the 'high' times below count from that moment. Lows and SDA steps are plain clock counts.
START on a free bus - SDA low, wait 2Q, SCL low, wait Q.
START on an owned bus (repeated START; SCL is low) - release SDA, wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, SDA low, wait 2Q, SCL low, wait Q. Never a STOP in between.
Each of the 9 bits of WRITE and READ - set SDA (0 = pull low, 1 = release), wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, sample SDA, SCL low, wait Q.
WRITE - 8 data bits MSB first, then the ACK bit with SDA released; STATUS.NACK = the SDA level sampled in the ACK bit.
READ - 8 bits with SDA released, sampled MSB first into RXDATA; then the ACK bit - SDA low for ACK, released for NACK.
STOP - SDA low, wait Q, release SCL and wait high, wait 2Q, release SDA, wait 2Q. Afterwards the bus is not owned.
SCL and SDA are only ever pulled low or released (high-Z); the output enables are registered.
STATUS.NACK is updated at the end of every WRITE and is otherwise unchanged (reset 0).
RXDATA is updated at the end of every READ (reset 0).

"""Acceptance tests of t2_i2c_cmd_master against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board
from benchmark.lib.i2c_devices import Adt7420, FixedDevice, I2cBus
from model import (BUSY, CMD, DESIGN_ID, INFO, OP_READ, OP_START, OP_STOP, OP_WRITE, OWNED, RXDATA, STATUS, Model,
                   cmd_word)

ADDR = 0x4B


# v1.2: SCL high time is 2Q to 2Q + SYNC_SLACK clocks. The spec says wait until SCL is seen high through a two-flop
# synchroniser, then 2Q: 2-3 clocks of synchroniser plus 1-3 of state and registered-output latency; 8 allows for that.
SYNC_SLACK = 8


class Env:
    def __init__(self, dut, temp_q7: int = 0x0D87) -> None:
        self.b = Board(dut, {"dev_scl_pull": 0, "dev_sda_pull": 0})
        self.dut = dut
        self.q = self.b.param("QUARTER")
        self.temp = temp_q7

    async def start(self) -> None:
        await self.b.start()
        self.bus = I2cBus(self.dut, [Adt7420(self.temp), FixedDevice(0x1D)])
        self.m = Model([Adt7420(self.temp), FixedDevice(0x1D)], self.q)

    async def cmd(self, op: int, data: int = 0, rnack: int = 0, check: bool = True) -> None:
        w = cmd_word(op, data, rnack)
        await self.b.write(CMD, w)
        self.m.command(w)
        if check:
            await self.regs()

    async def regs(self) -> None:
        for off, name in ((STATUS, "STATUS"), (RXDATA, "RXDATA")):
            await self.b.expect(off, self.m.read(off), name)

    def check_bus(self) -> None:
        assert not self.bus.errors, self.bus.errors[:3]
        assert self.bus.log == self.m.log, f"bus {self.bus.log} != model {self.m.log}"

    async def reg_read(self, ptr: int, n: int, addr: int = ADDR) -> None:
        await self.cmd(OP_START)
        await self.cmd(OP_WRITE, addr << 1)
        await self.cmd(OP_WRITE, ptr)
        await self.cmd(OP_START)
        await self.cmd(OP_WRITE, addr << 1 | 1)
        for i in range(n):
            await self.cmd(OP_READ, rnack=int(i == n - 1))
        await self.cmd(OP_STOP)


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1171060, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    assert await e.b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    await e.regs()
    for off in (CMD, INFO, 0x04, 0x7F):
        await e.b.expect(off, e.m.read(off), f"window 0x{off:02X}")
    assert int(dut.scl.value) == 1 and int(dut.sda.value) == 1, "bus not released after reset"
    e.check_bus()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1536840, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_id_via_repeated_start(dut):
    """Trap: the pointer write must be followed by a repeated START, never a STOP: this ADT7420 loses its pointer on
    a STOP (a master that sends STOP before every START reads register 0x00 instead of the ID)."""
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.reg_read(0x0B, 1)
    assert e.m.rxdata == 0xCB
    await e.b.expect(RXDATA, 0xCB, "ID register")
    e.check_bus()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2244040, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_temperature_two_bytes(dut):
    e = Env(dut, temp_q7=-0x0123)
    await e.start()
    await e.reg_read(0x00, 2)
    await e.reg_read(0x02, 3)
    e.check_bus()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=2317200, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_write_then_read_back(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, ADDR << 1)
    for b in (0x04, 0x1A, 0x80, 0x0C, 0x40):        # pointer T_HIGH, then T_HIGH and T_LOW, auto-increment
        await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, b)
    await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
    await e.reg_read(0x04, 4)
    e.check_bus()
    assert e.bus.devices[0].writes == [(0x04, 0x1A), (0x05, 0x80), (0x06, 0x0C), (0x07, 0x40)]


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1512440, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_nack_address(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, 0x48 << 1)                # no device at 0x48
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, 0x00)                     # still NACK: nobody listening
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, 0x1D << 1 | 1)            # another device ACKs
    await e.cmd(OP_READ, rnack=1)
    await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
    e.check_bus()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1611200, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_clock_stretching(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, ADDR << 1)
    e.bus.stretch_next = 300                        # the sensor holds SCL low for 300 clocks once
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, 0x0B)
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, ADDR << 1 | 1)
    e.bus.stretch_next = 2500                       # longer than a shell access: commands meanwhile are ignored
    await e.b.write(CMD, cmd_word(OP_READ, rnack=1))
    e.m.command(cmd_word(OP_READ, rnack=1))
    await e.b.write(CMD, cmd_word(OP_STOP))         # ignored: busy
    await e.b.expect(STATUS, BUSY | OWNED, "STATUS while busy")
    await e.b.cycles(2500)
    await e.regs()
    await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
    e.check_bus()
    hi = 2 * e.q
    assert all(hi <= h <= hi + SYNC_SLACK for h in e.bus.high), f"SCL high times {sorted(set(e.bus.high))}, 2Q = {hi}"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1585600, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_bit_timing(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.reg_read(0x00, 2)
    e.check_bus()
    hi, lo = 2 * e.q, 2 * e.q
    assert e.bus.high and all(hi <= h <= hi + SYNC_SLACK for h in e.bus.high), f"SCL high {sorted(set(e.bus.high))}"
    inner = [t for t in e.bus.low if t < 100]            # lows inside a command (between commands SCL waits low)
    assert len(inner) >= 8 * 5 and all(lo <= t <= lo + 2 for t in inner), f"SCL low {sorted(set(e.bus.low))}"


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=1857840, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_ignored_commands(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for w in (cmd_word(OP_WRITE, 0x96), cmd_word(OP_READ), cmd_word(OP_STOP), 0, 5, 6, 7):
        await e.b.write(CMD, w)                     # free bus: nothing happens
        e.m.command(w)
        await e.regs()
    await e.b.cycles(200)
    e.check_bus()
    assert e.bus.log == []
    await e.cmd(OP_START)
    await e.b.write(CMD, 0x0005)                    # invalid OP on an owned bus
    await e.regs()
    await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
    await e.b.write(0x02, 0x55)                     # read-only registers
    await e.b.write(0x03, 0x55)
    await e.regs()
    await e.b.expect(INFO, e.q, "INFO")
    e.check_bus()


@cocotb.test(timeout_time=3487760, timeout_unit="ns")
async def test_random_transactions(dut):
    e = Env(dut, temp_q7=0x0B4F)
    await e.start()
    rng = random.Random(int(cocotb.RANDOM_SEED))
    for _ in range(5):
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.45:
            await e.reg_read(rng.choice([0x00, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x06, 0x0A, 0x0B]), rng.randrange(1, 4))
        elif r < 0.75:
            await e.cmd(OP_START)
            await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, ADDR << 1)
            ptr = rng.choice([0x04, 0x06, 0x08, 0x0A])
            await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, ptr)
            for _ in range(rng.randrange(1, 3)):
                await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, rng.randrange(256))
            await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
        else:
            await e.cmd(OP_START)
            await e.cmd(OP_WRITE, rng.choice([0x10, 0x48, 0x4A, 0x77]) << 1 | rng.randrange(2))
            await e.cmd(OP_STOP)
    e.check_bus()

requirements.text: START, repeated START, WRITE, READ and STOP produce the listed waveforms; a START on an owned bus is a repeated START
WRITE records ACK/NACK; READ returns the byte and answers ACK or NACK as told
Clock stretching is honoured - every SCL high time counts from SCL seen high
The lines are never driven high
Commands while busy, invalid OPs and data commands on a free bus are ignored
On the board the ADT7420 at 0x4B answers its ID 0xCB through a pointer write, repeated START and read
The design closes timing at 100 MHz with no unconstrained path

resources_expected: about a hundred LUTs and FFs; no BRAM, no DSP
spec_md:
# Byte-command I2C master on the temperature-sensor bus

I want to talk to the Nexys A7-100T's on-board I2C bus (the ADT7420 temperature sensor's TMP_SCL / TMP_SDA) from a
script, one bus operation at a time, so I can try any register sequence without rebuilding the FPGA.

- Four commands I can issue over the test shell: START, WRITE a byte, READ a byte, STOP. A START while I already
  have the bus must come out as a repeated START. A WRITE records whether the slave acknowledged. A READ is told
  whether to answer ACK (more to come) or NACK (last byte).
- Status shows busy and whether the last written byte was NACKed; the last byte read is in a register.
- The lines are open drain with the board's pull-ups: never drive them high. Slaves may stretch the clock and the
  master must wait for them.
- SCL speed: set by a parameter giving a quarter of the SCL period in clocks (equal high and low halves); on the
  board I'd like 100 kHz.
- Design ID "I2CM".

Test hooks: top module `t2_i2c_cmd_master_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC (`TMP_SCL`, `TMP_SDA`,
the USB-UART pins, `CLK100MHZ`, `CPU_RESETN`), the test shell's `CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP`
parameters, plus `QUARTER` (a quarter of the SCL period, in clocks) as top-level parameters.
title: Byte-command I2C master on the temperature-sensor bus

captions: Command 0: START - START on a free bus.
Command 1: WRITE - the address byte 0x96 (device 0x4b, write): acknowledged.
Command 3: START - a repeated START (the master already holds the bus, so no STOP in between).
Command 4: WRITE - the address byte 0x97 (device 0x4b, read): acknowledged.
Command 5: READ - reads byte 0xcb and answers NACK, the last byte.
Command 6: STOP - STOP, the bus is free again.
Command 7: START - START on a free bus.
Command 8: WRITE - the address byte 0x3b (device 0x1d, read): acknowledged.
Command 9: READ - reads byte 0xff and answers NACK, the last byte.
Command 10: STOP - STOP, the bus is free again.
Command 11: START - START on a free bus.
Command 12: WRITE - the address byte 0xa0 (device 0x50, write): not acknowledged.
Command 13: STOP - STOP, the bus is free again.
trace.stimulus: A script of 14 commands: read the sensor's ID register (pointer write, repeated START, one read), read one byte from a second device at 0x1D, then address a device that is not there.

what: An I2C bus master that is controlled one bus operation at a time from the test shell. The user can issue a start, write a byte, read a byte or send a stop, and a start while the bus is already held becomes a repeated start. The design records whether each written byte was acknowledged and keeps the last byte read. The lines are open drain, so it only ever pulls them low or lets go, and it waits whenever a slave holds the clock low.
where: I2C is the common two-wire bus for sensors, memory chips, real-time clocks, display controllers and power-management chips. A command-level master like this is what bring-up tools use to poke at a part before any driver exists.
